title: External cervical resorption on CBCT
topic: ECR enters below the epithelial attachment, spreads around a canal walled off by a resistant sheet, and looks smaller on 2-D films.

claims.claim: Initiation: entry at the cervical root surface, just below the epithelial attachment
claims.source: Mavridou et al., J Endod 2016;42:1737-1751 (PMID 27776885) - abstract ('initiated at the cementum below the gingival epithelial attachment'); 'just below': Patel et al., Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - full text ('immediately below the epithelial attachment')

claims.claim: Resorption spreads around the canal (circumferentially and apico-coronally)
claims.source: Patel et al., Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - full text ('spreading circumferentially and apico-coronally', credited there to the 3-stage model of Mavridou 2016); Chen et al., J Endod 2021;47:883-894 (PMID 33745945) - abstract ('extends apicocoronally and circumferentially inside the dentin'); histology base and on-screen source line: Mavridou et al., J Endod 2016;42:1737-1751 (PMID 27776885) - abstract (3-D invasion toward the pulp space, stopped by the pericanalar sheet; the abstract itself does not use the word circumferential)

claims.claim: Pulp walled off - until late - by a resorption-resistant sheet; chip 'avg ~0.2 mm, ex vivo' is shown only while the Mavridou source line is on screen (8.3-13.2 s)
claims.source: Mavridou et al., J Endod 2016;42:1737-1751 (PMID 27776885) - abstract: pericanalar resorption-resistant sheet of predentin, dentin and occasionally bone-like tissue, 'fluctuating thickness averaging 210 um' (study of 27 extracted vital teeth; number of teeth measured not stated); 'until late': Heithersay, Quintessence Int 1999;30:27-37 (PMID 10323156) - abstract ('protected by a thin layer of predentin until late in the process'); Patel et al., Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - full text ('Only in advanced cases does the ECR lesion perforate into the root canal')

claims.claim: Repair: bone-like tissue grows in while resorption continues elsewhere (proposed 3-stage model: initiation, resorption, repair)
claims.source: Mavridou et al., J Endod 2016;42:1737-1751 (PMID 27776885) - abstract

claims.claim: Patel 3-D classification: height 1-4; spread A <=90, B <=180, C <=270, D >270 degrees; proximity d (dentin only) / p (probable pulp; in full: probable pulpal involvement, a CBCT judgment, not proof of perforation)
claims.source: Patel et al., Int Endod J 2018;51:206-214 (PMID 28746776) - abstract

Patel K et al., J Endod 2016;42:1435-1440 (PMID 27507628) - abstract ('PRs also underestimated the size of the ECR lesion'; 115 consecutively diagnosed teeth in 98 patients, CBCT as comparator); on-screen source line 'Underestimation: Patel K et al., J Endod 2016'

claims.claim: Canal outline often still traceable on the periapical
claims.source: Heithersay, Quintessence Int 1999;30:27-37 (PMID 10323156) - abstract ('generally'); Patel et al., Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - full text ('root canal outline is visible as long as there is no perforation'; this is the source line on the end card, where the chip is still lit); 'often' rather than 'always' because Luso & Luder, Schweiz Monatsschr Zahnmed 2012;122:914-930 (PMID 23097140) - abstract: frequently not recognizable on conventional films. Not from Patel K 2016

claims.claim: Take-home: recognize it early; consider CBCT before you treat; treatment depends on extent
claims.source: Patel et al., Int Endod J 2022;55 Suppl 4:892-921 (PMID 35229320) - full text (on-screen source line): 'CBCT should be considered prior to managing ECR'; 'Management of ECR depends on the nature and accessibility of the lesion'; Patel K et al., J Endod 2016;42:1435-1440 (PMID 27507628) - abstract ('A CBCT scan should be considered before the management of a potentially restorable ECR lesion'); Patel et al., Int Endod J 2018;51:1224-1238 (PMID 29737544) - abstract (management chosen by extent and access); 'early': Heithersay, Quintessence Int 1999;30:96-110 (PMID 10356561) - abstract ('Diagnosis of lesions at an early stage is ... highly desirable')

claims.claim: Toy model / schematic: procedural CBCT volume of a single-rooted tooth; lesion shape and timing, the ~233 degree reading, height zone 2 and the class '2Cp' describe the drawn model, not a patient; the sheet is drawn as a uniform band thicker than 0.2 mm; the orange 'extent on CBCT' outline is the model's projected lesion, larger than the visible radiolucency by an invented detection threshold (no size ratio implied)
claims.source: Original schematic (labeled 'SCHEMATIC - not a patient scan - not to scale' on screen for the whole reel)

caption:
External cervical resorption, as CBCT shows it.
Enters just below the epithelial attachment, spreads AROUND the canal: a thin resistant sheet (avg ~0.2 mm, ex vivo) walls off the pulp until late.
On CBCT a lesion against the canal is coded "p" (probable pulp involvement, Patel 2018): a scan judgment, not proof of perforation; a thin sheet often still separates the two.
Periapicals underestimate it: consider CBCT before you treat.
Schematic animation, not a patient scan.
Refs: Mavridou 2016, J Endod 42:1737; Heithersay 1999, Quintessence Int 30:27; Patel 2018, Int Endod J 51:206; Patel 2022, Int Endod J 55(S4):892; Patel K 2016, J Endod 42:1435.
